lines.text: Good evening, friends, and welcome back to American Family Field for Game Two of the World Series. The Milwaukee Brewers hold a one to zero lead in this series after a close three to two win in the opener. Logan Henderson gets the ball for Milwaukee tonight, while Drew Rasmussen toes the rubber for the Tampa Bay Rays. Glad you could join us on the porch as the autumn air settles in over Wisconsin.

Logan Henderson gets the ball for Milwaukee tonight, the twenty-four year old right-hander from Houston making his first postseason turn after breaking into the big leagues just this year. Standing six feet even on the mound, young Logan has quite a task ahead against Drew Rasmussen. Rasmussen is thirty-one, hailing from Puyallup, Washington, and standing six foot one, with his major league service dating back to twenty twenty.

Yandy Díaz steps up, Aranita Diaz, looking sharp with that Cuban fire. Henderson fires a four-seam fastball, 94, foul. Count’s now 0 balls, 1 strike. The kid’s got a fresh start, just like he did in his first game.
The four-seam fastball, 94, clips the outside corner, foul. Count’s now 0 balls, 2 strikes. Yandy Díaz stays set, eyes on the plate, the pitcher’s rhythm steady as he works through the count.
Henderson delivers a four-seam fastball, 95, soft inside, good bounce. Ball, count’s now 1 ball, 2 strikes. Yandy Díaz stays rooted, eyes locked, the plate still just ahead.
Henderson fires a changeup, 84, soft and slow, ball. Count’s now 2 balls, 2 strikes. Yandy Díaz stays square, hands down, the pitch just shy of the zone, the count hanging there, waiting to settle.
with the count 2 and 2: Four-Seam Fastball 93 mph, foul, making the count 2 and 2
Reminds me of my single summer in Class A ball where I caught so many foul tips my glove turned into sawdust. Henderson winds and deals.

Cutter 86, foul, count still 2 balls, 2 strikes. Yandy Díaz stays square, eyes on the plate, Henderson's delivery calm, the pitch just outside, the count holding tight, no rush, no shift—just the silence between pitches, like a breath before the next one.
The Brewers haven’t scored yet, just like they didn’t in Game 1, when they pulled off a three-run win to take the series lead. Tonight, it’s still 0–0.

Henderson delivers the changeup, Yandy Díaz taps it slow on the dirt, shortstop Cooper Pratt throws it wide of first, and Díaz hustles all the way to second on the error with nobody out and no score yet.
Corbin Burnes won the Cy Young Award in twenty twenty-one, the Brewers' first since Pete Vuckovich.

Four-Seam Fastball 94 mph, called strike, making the count 0 and 1. Aranda steps back, ready to go, Henderson's first pitch crisp and clean. Second base is live, but no pressure yet. Score still tied, 0–0.

Cutter 88 mph, foul, count now 0 balls and 2 strikes. Aranda stays steady, eyes locked on the plate, Henderson's windup smooth, glove tucked close, bat held low—just waiting for that next one to come in.

Ninety-six mile per hour four-seam fastball fouled away, the count holding firm at zero and two. Henderson stays calm out there on the mound with a runner waiting on second and nobody out in a scoreless game.
Henderson’s got seven pitches on the board, six of them strikes, and he’s been in the post season with a 3.00 ERA and six strikeouts in two games so far.

Henderson looks in, ninety-six miles per hour on the outside corner and Aranda chases it, swinging through the last one Got him on the high heat, that is one away right there with the runner still parked on second and nobody crossing the plate yet.

Chandler Simpson swings at the four-seam fastball, 95 mph, makes contact with the bat, the ball sails up the middle, just over the infield grass, and drops in fair territory. Count becomes one ball and zero strikes. Runner on second stays put, no play made. Score still dead even, 0–0.
One out, runners on second, series tied 1-0, Brewers leading after Game 1, Simpson’s got a chance to make his mark.
Henderson looks for the sign, comes home with a ninety-four mile per hour four-seam fastball, Simpson fouls it off the other way, and the count stands at one ball and one strike.
Simpson's up with a runner on second, Henderson's on the mound with a 3.00 ERA, and the outfielders are watching for any pop-ups or deep drives — keep an eye on the gaps, especially left-center.

Henderson checks the runner on second, deals a ninety-four mile per hour fastball, Simpson grounds it out to center, Díaz comes home with the game's first run Oh, you have got to be kidding me, right up the middle and the Brewers fall behind one to nothing!
Changeup, eighty-four miles per hour, called strike. Count now one ball, one strike. Junior Caminero up, one out, runner on first, Rays lead one to nothing. Henderson sets the stage, ready to go.
Henderson starts with a changeup, eighty-five miles per hour, called strike. Count now zero balls, two strikes. Caminero works the count, one out, runners on first, Rays leading one to nothing.

Henderson sets the scene with a four-seam fastball, ninety-six miles per hour, ball lands in the zone, count now one ball and two strikes. Caminero stays on the plate, eyes locked on the plate, ready for what comes next.

Henderson fires a four-seam fastball, ninety-five miles per hour, ball lands in the zone, count now two balls and two strikes. Caminero stays on the plate, eyes fixed, ready for the next one. One out, runners on first, Rays lead one to nothing.
Caminero's on the plate with two balls and two strikes, one out, runners on first, Brewers need a hit to tie the series.
Chandler Simpson sprints to second, one out, runners on first. Caminero stays on the plate, eyes fixed.
Cutter, eighty-six miles per hour, foul. Count still two balls and two strikes. Caminero stays on the plate, eyes fixed, ready for the next one. One out, runners on first, Rays lead one to nothing.
Caminero swings at the cutter, eighty-eight miles per hour, ball drops in the dirt. Count now three balls and two strikes. One out, runners on first, Rays lead one to nothing.
Next up’s Junior Caminero, got a .278 clip this post-season, still got a chance to turn this series around with a good swing.

Foul tip off the bat, Henderson fires a four-seam fastball, ninety-four miles per hour, count remains three balls and two strikes. Caminero stays on the plate, eyes fixed, one out, runners on first, Rays lead one to nothing.
Cecil Cooper drove in more than a hundred runs three times for Milwaukee.
Changeup, eighty-six miles per hour, fouls off, count stays 3 balls and 2 strikes. Caminero stays on the plate, eyes fixed, one out, runners on first, Rays lead one to nothing.
Junior’s got that .278 swing going, pulled a home run in Game 3 back in the playoffs, still got a shot to turn this series around.

Henderson comes back with an eighty-four mile per hour changeup, Caminero swings and taps a ground ball out toward left fielder Jackson Chourio, a ninety-nine mile per hour hit dropping just fair Oh no, he loops it right into the grass and Simpson scampers home with another run, goodness gracious me, that's two for Tampa Bay!
Henderson takes the mound visit, checks the signs, keeps the rhythm going.

Henderson winds up, gloves the ball, throws it out there, Hicks swings and the four-seam fastball bites the barrel — foul. Count now stands at zero balls, one strike. One out, runners on first, Rays lead two to nothing.
Runners on first, one out, Rays up 2 to nothing—first inning’s been tight, but the Brewers haven’t cracked it yet, just like they didn’t in Game 1.

Henderson looks in for signs, checks the runner, and deals an eighty-eight mile per hour cutter Hicks lifts it high to right center, oh goodness me it is carrying and gone into the seats, a four-run lead for Tampa Bay!
Palacios steps in, Henderson fires a four-seam fastball at 94, right on the plate — called strike. Count now stands at zero balls, one strike. One out, bases empty, Rays lead 4 to 0.

Zero balls, two strikes. Palacios swings at the eighty-five mile per hour changeup, misses inside, it's a swinging strike. The count is now zero balls, two strikes. One out, bases empty, Rays leading 4 to 0.
Henderson’s on the mound, Palacios at second, gotta watch for any pop to right—tight spot, no room to play wide.
Palacios takes a step, Henderson fires a changeup at 86, it floats just outside the zone — ball. Count now stands at one ball, two strikes. One out, bases empty, Rays lead 4 to 0.

Right into the catcher's mitt. Logan Henderson comes right back with the eighty-five mile per hour changeup, Palacios swings through it for the second out of the inning! Henderson rings him up, way to battle back and shut the door right there!

The pitch floats just over the plate, called strike, count now stands at zero balls, one strike. Two out, bases empty, Rays lead 4 to 0. DeLuca’s got a solid start, hasn’t cracked the order yet this postseason.

Jonny DeLuca steps in, Henderson fires a four-seam fastball at 94, right on the plate — called strike. Count now stands at zero balls, two strikes. Two out, bases empty, Rays lead 4 to 0. DeLuca’s got a solid start, hasn’t cracked the order yet this postseason.

The Brewers lead the series 1 to 0, and they’ve not lost a game yet. DeLuca’s got a cold start, hitting just .176 in this post season so far. Henderson’s got a shaky line, but he’s keeping the Rays off the board.
with the count 0 and 2: Changeup 84 mph, ball, making the count 1 and 2
DeLuca steps up with one ball, two strikes, trying to shake off the cold streak, while Henderson stays tight, needing just one more to keep the Rays' lead intact.

Henderson comes back with a changeup, eighty-four miles per hour, foul tip, the count stays at one ball, two strikes. DeLuca works the count, needs one more to move on, Henderson stays calm, ready for the next pitch.
Henderson fires a four-seam fastball at 94, foul tip, count stays at one ball, two strikes. DeLuca works the count, needs one more to move on, Henderson stays calm, ready for the next pitch.
Robin Yount reached the big leagues at eighteen and played all twenty of his seasons in Milwaukee.

Henderson delivers the eighty-three mile per hour changeup, DeLuca lifts a line drive out to left fielder Jackson Chourio, who pulls it in for the third out, and after half an inning, Tampa Bay four, Milwaukee zero.

Well that brings us to the end of the top half, with Tampa Bay jumping out to four runs on three hits, leaving our boys looking for their first baserunner. It is the first World Series here in town since nineteen eighty-two, and we are still chasing that elusive first title. Time to see our bats get to work as we stretch our legs and wait for the bottom of the first.

Every great team needs a utility man, and for your tech, that's Josh Stutting. Networks, computers, a little artificial intelligence wizardry. stutting dot josh at gmail dot com. That's s, t, u, t, t, i, n, g, dot, j, o, s, h, at gmail dot com.
DeLuca steps to the plate carrying a batting average of one seventy six over ten games this postseason, looking to spark some life after that four run top half.

Rasmussen fires a sharp 88 mile per hour cutter, called strike one. Count now stands at zero balls, one strike. Chourio, just 22, made his debut in '24, showing promise with a .205 clip this postseason. He’s got the eyes, but this one’s tight.

Rasmussen looks in, brings the eighty-nine mile per hour cutter to the plate, and Chourio meets it on the ground out toward right field. He's safe with a single and our boys have their very first hit of the night right here in the bottom of the first!

Runners on first, no outs, count at one ball zero strikes. Bauers takes a 93 mile per hour sinker, swings and makes contact, the ball drops soft to the dirt in right field. Count now stands at one ball, zero strikes.

Count's at two balls, zero strikes. Rasmussen fires a 87 mile per hour cutter, it stays low and just misses the plate, ball. Bauers, known as JB, stays calm, takes a breath, and waits for the next one.
Rasmussen’s been steady so far, two pitches tossed, keeping the count even with a solid command out of the zone.

Right to the glove of Victor Mesa Jr out in right field on a sharp grounder off the bat at one hundred five miles per hour Bauers shoots one through and our boys have got something cooking now with runners parked at the corners and nobody out in the first!

Count now stands at zero balls, one strike. Yelich, the big man from Thousand Oaks, takes a look at the plate, eyes locked on Rasmussen’s four-seam, 96 mile per hour heater. That one’s right on the edge.
Yelich takes a look at the plate, eyes on Rasmussen’s changeup, 88 mile per hour, it brushes the outside corner, ball. Count now stands at one ball, one strike.
Yelich swings at Rasmussen’s 95 mile per hour sinker, pulls it foul, the ball cracks into the gap near the wall. Count now stands at one ball, two strikes.
Mesa in right, watching for anything low to the ground, and Chourio up near the fence, gotta keep an eye on that line drive from Yelich.

Rasmussen settles in, fires a changeup at 89 miles per hour, it lands just outside, ball. Count now stands at two balls, two strikes. Yelich waits, eyes on the plate, the count balanced, the moment hangs there.

Rasmussen comes set, deals a ninety-six mile per hour four-seam fastball, Yelich swings through it and goes down swinging for the first out with runners still parked at the corners and our boys trailing four to nothing.

Yelich, thirty-four years old, from Thousand Oaks, got his first taste of the majors in '13 — now he's in the World Series, looking to make a mark with his patience and a little more than a .286 average.
Contreras takes a peek at the plate, Rasmussen fires a 91 mile per hour cutter, it bounces just wide, ball. Count now stands at one ball, zero strikes.
CC Sabathia came to Milwaukee in a midseason trade in two thousand eight and pitched the Brewers into their first postseason in twenty-six years.

Mesa in right, keeping an eye on that corner, Rasmussen fires a 97 mile per hour four-seam fastball, Contreras swings and misses foul, count now stands at one ball, one strike. Contreras, 28, from Puerto Cabello, has been hot this post-season, hitting .394 with three homers.

The Rays have all the runs so far, scoring four in the first, while our boys haven't had a hit yet. One out, runners on first and third, and we're still sitting at zero. Contreras waits, the count balanced.
Rasmussen fires a 97 mile per hour sinker, it curls just outside, ball. Count now stands at two balls, one strike. Contreras waits, the count balanced, looking for the next pitch.

Drew Rasmussen steps back on the rubber, peers in for the sign, and delivers a ninety-two mile per hour cutter, Contreras swings right through it and now the count sits at two balls and two strikes with one down.
Runners on first and third, one out, count at three balls, two strikes. Contreras faces Rasmussen, the cutter drops in the dirt, ball. Count now stands at three balls, three strikes.
One out, runners on first and third, Contreras with the count at three balls, two strikes—still needs one more to make it even, and Rasmussen’s got a steady hand on the mound.

Contreras works the full count against Rasmussen, waiting on that ninety-six mile per hour sinker right down there and he grounds it softly out to center, Jackson Chourio trots home with our very first run!
Rasmussen checks the mound, adjusts his glove, goes back to the plate. Contreras waits, count balanced.
Turang takes the plate, Rasmussen fires a 89 mile per hour cutter, ball, count now stands at one ball, zero strikes. Runners on first and third, one out, situation tight.

Turang standing in at six feet tall, born out in Corona, California, he waits as Rasmussen winds and unleashes an eighty-nine mile per hour changeup, missing the zone, ball, making the count two balls and zero strikes.

Brice Turang steps in, lefty, first time today, count at zero, zero. Rasmussen fires a cutter, ball, then a changeup, ball, and a cutter in play—contact off the bat, line drive, 108 mph, 148 feet, lines out to second. Two outs, runners on first and third, Rays lead 4 to 1.
The Brewers lead the series 1 to 0, and with one more run tonight, we might just turn this around. Brice Turang’s first at-bat’s a big one for him, and for us.
Mitchell steps in, 6 foot 2, Orange, CA born, waits on that 96 mile per hour sinker, ball, count now stands at one ball, zero strikes. Two out, runners on first and third, Rays lead 4 to 1.
Rasmussen’s been working steady, 19 pitches so far, keeping the series edge in check with that 1.29 ERA through three games.
Rasmussen comes back with a ninety mile per hour changeup, missing down low, and the count climbs now to two balls and no strikes, with the ducks still out there on the corners.
Garrett Mitchell swings at the 90 mile per hour cutter, swings hard, makes contact, it's a swinging strike, count now 2 balls and 1 strike. Two outs, runners on first and third, Rays lead 4 to 1.
Cutter, ball, count now 3 and 1. Mitchell stays on the plate, Rasmussen's been sharp, two outs, runners on first and third, Rays lead 4 to 1. The Brewers need to answer that one.
Sinker, 96 mile per hour, called strike. Count now 3 and 2. Mitchell stays on the plate, two outs, runners on first and third, Rays lead 4 to 1. Rasmussen’s been sharp, keeping the pressure on.
The ball in glove logo came back as the Brewers' main logo in twenty twenty.

Full count still, Rasmussen brings the ninety-eight mile per hour four-seam fastball, fouled straight back. Count remains three and two, two away, runners at the corners, Brewers down four to one here in the first.
That reminds me of my three weeks in the low minors when my throw to second once hit the mascot. Rasmussen stares in, deals.

Full count on Mitchell, Rasmussen delivers an eighty-nine mile per hour changeup, line drive down toward right Mitchell drives it safely into right field for a sharp single, Bauers jogs home with a run, and the Brewers cut into the lead with two men down, now trailing four to two

Cooper Pratt comes to the plate, count 0 and 1, Rasmussen fires a 91 mile per hour cutter, called strike. The young shortstop, just 22, steps up with some promise, two out, runners on first and third, Brewers trying to respond in the bottom of the first.

Rasmussen winds up, glove in hand, fires a 97 mile per hour four-seam fastball, foul tip over the right-field line. Count now 0 and 2. Two outs, runners on first and third, Brewers still trailing 4 to 2.
Two outs, runners on first and third, Brewers got one run in the first, now tied at two apiece after the Rays had all four early. That’s how the series stands, one to zero for Milwaukee.

Rasmussen gets the sign from the catcher, steps back on the rubber, and delivers the pitch on zero and two He swings and misses for the third out, oh my goodness gracious how do you chase that high heater way out of the zone, the inning is over and the Brewers leave two stranded leaving it four to two

Well that brings a lively first frame to a close here at the ballpark with the Brewers pushing across two runs on four hits to claw right back into it. Tampa Bay four and Milwaukee two as we step aside for a moment.
Folks, the real all star in this booth is Josh Stutting. He's batting a thousand on tech problems. Look him up: stutting dot josh at gmail dot com.
Cooper Pratt settles back into the box now, the young shortstop carrying a batting average of two hundred eighty-one through nine postseason games.

Victor Mesa Jr. takes the plate, looks down at the mound, Henderson fires a 83 mile per hour changeup, sharp and quick, called strike one. Count now 0 and 1. Bases empty, top of the second, Rays lead 4 to 2.
Series stands 1 to 0 for the Brewers, and they’ve done it without losing a game — just like in Game 1, when they edged out the Rays 3 to 2. Tonight’s early push keeps hope alive.
with the count 0 and 1: Changeup 84 mph, ball, making the count 1 and 1
Count 1-1, no outs, bases empty. Mesa Jr. looking to spark something with a .147 average, Henderson working through his 35th pitch.
Henderson winds up, glove ready, fires a four-seam fastball 94 miles per hour, ball, count now 2 and 1. Mesa Jr. stays calm, eyes on the plate, no pressure yet, just waiting for the next one.
Henderson checks the grip, uncorking a ninety-three mile per hour four-seam fastball that misses wide, pushing the count to three and one on the twenty-five-year-old outfielder Mesa Jr.
Mesa Jr. stands there, 25 years old, Cuban roots, just .147 so far—still got a chance to make a mark, just like the first time he stepped onto a big league field.
Mesa Jr. takes a ninety-three mile per hour fastball well off the plate for ball four, walking down to first base and putting a runner on for Tampa Bay, keeping the score four to two in the second.
The Rays have all the runs so far, two in the second, with a fourth in the first — but the Brewers aren’t out of it yet, they’ve got a chance to keep this series alive.
Henderson fires a 93-mile-per-hour four-seam fastball, Walls fouls it back to the plate, count now 0 and 1. No outs, runner on first, Brewers still clinging to a two-run deficit.
Ryan Braun is the Brewers' all-time home run leader.

Henderson looks in, delivers an eighty-five mile per hour changeup, Walls drops a bunt down the line, Henderson gloves it and flips to first for the out, moving the runner up as the score stays four to two in the second.
Henderson's on the mound, Walls at shortstop, second base is live — they'll be watching for a pop-up or a hard ground ball down the line, with the count fresh at zero, and one out, runners on second.

Henderson sets up, gloves close, fires a changeup at 87 miles an hour — sharp and clean — Díaz meets it with a quick swing, the ball snaps into the strike zone, count now 0 and 1. One out, runners on second, still a tight game.
with the count 0 and 1: Changeup 86 mph, foul, making the count 0 and 2
The ball popped up just shy of the infield grass, Henderson’s night’s fourth pitch, still working through his first two innings without a strikeout.

Díaz meets the four-seam fastball with a quick lift, the ball lands just outside the box, count now 1 and 2. One out, runners on second, still a tight game. Henderson keeps the ball tight, ready for the next pitch.
Runners on second, one out, count at 1 ball and 2 strikes, Díaz looking to move the game with a swing, Henderson holding steady, still got work to do in his first two innings.

Henderson grips the ball, peering past the runner on second base, and delivers the ninety-six mile per hour four-seam fastball Díaz swings through it and Logan Henderson gets his strikeout right there, what a beauty of a pitch to finish him off and two down now in the second with the score still four to two Rays
Aranda swings at the 96 mile per hour four-seam fastball, makes contact, the ball drops just outside the box, count now 1 and 0. Two out, runners on second, Rays lead 4 to 2, still a tight game.

Aranda faces Henderson with a 86 mile per hour changeup, foul, count now 1 and 1. Two out, runners on second, Rays lead 4 to 2, still a tight game. Henderson keeps the ball tight, ready for the next pitch.
with the count 1 and 1: Changeup 84 mph, swinging strike, making the count 1 and 2
Aranda’s been hitting .316 this postseason, good for a solid start, though he’s gone 0 for 1 so far tonight. Just keep that eye on the plate, kid.

The changeup drops just outside the box, 82 miles per hour, foul. Count stays at 1 and 2. Aranda's working through the count, still looking for a clean one, two outs, runners on second, Rays lead 4 to 2.

Henderson works from the stretch now, checking that runner on second and firing the fastball toward the plate and Aranda swings right through it for the third out, Logan Henderson gets the big strikeout to strand them, let's go

And that takes care of the top half of the second inning, folks, with Tampa Bay still holding a four to two lead over our Milwaukee boys. Let us grab a cold root beer from the icebox while we change sides.
Bob's Booth is made possible by Josh Stutting, the five tool player of tech: he fixes it, builds it, automates it, explains it, and does it with a smile. stutting dot josh at gmail dot com.
Right into the catcher's mitt. Tampa Bay put up four in the opening frame, and our boys answered with two of their own in the bottom half.

Frelick swings at the 94 mile per hour sinker, makes contact, it’s a ball, count goes to one and zero. Bottom of the second, bases empty, Rays up 4 to 2, Frelick coming off a .222 line in the post season.
Frelick takes a crack at the 91 mile per hour cutter, Rasmussen sets it up just over the plate, it’s called a strike, count now stands at one and one. Bases empty, Rays up 4 to 2.
Rasmussen peers in from the mound, comes set, and fires a ninety-six mile per hour four-seam fastball that Sal fouls away just out of reach, and the count now sits at one ball and two strikes.

Rasmussen looks in from the mound, comes set, and fires a ninety-five mile per hour sinker that misses the zone, and the count now moves to two balls and two strikes with nobody out in the bottom of the second inning and our boys still trailing four to two.
Rasmussen winds and deals the eighty-nine mile per hour changeup, Frelick lines it out to center fielder Jonny DeLuca for the out, one down in the second, Rays still leading four to two.

Frelick's up, Rasmussen's on the mound, outfielders gotta watch that center field gap—Sal's got a long stride, might try to pull one, and with the wind at his back, it could carry farther than expected.

David Hamilton comes to the plate, count at zero and zero, Rasmussen sets him up with a 95 mile per hour four-seam fastball that clips the outside corner, foul pop, now it's zero and one. He's been hot this post-season, .462, six hits in thirteen, one homer, two RBIs over five games.
David Hamilton waits for the next one, Rasmussen deals a ninety-six mile per hour four-seam fastball, Hamilton swings and misses, zero and two now, one away, our boys down by two in the second.
Hank Aaron hit the last of his seven hundred fifty-five home runs as a Brewer in nineteen seventy-six.

Rasmussen delivers the ninety-seven mile per hour four-seam fastball, Hamilton lifts it out to left fielder Chandler Simpson for the catch, two down in the second inning with our boys still trailing four to two.

Outfielders watching that center field gap, Sal’s got a long stride, might try to pull one, and with the wind at his back, it could carry farther than expected. Oh, I nearly got a start in the low minors where I tried to catch a fly ball with my mitt and ended up catching a squirrel instead. That was 1

Chourio comes up, count at zero and zero, Rasmussen fires a 97 mile per hour four-seam fastball that bites the outside corner, foul pop, now it's zero and one. Young kid from Maracaibo, just got his first hit in the post-season, still working on the rhythm.

Jackson Chourio comes to the plate, count at zero and one, Rasmussen fires a 96 mile per hour sinker that clips the inside corner, called strike, now it's zero and two. He's new to this post-season, just getting his feet under him.

Chourio's got a fresh look at the plate, count at zero and two, two outs, bases empty. The Brewers want to tie this one, Rays need to keep their lead. Fresh legs, first time in the post-season since he got that first hit.

Bases empty here in the bottom of the second inning with our boys down four to two, Rasmussen deals an eighty-nine mile per hour cutter that misses outside, one ball and two strikes now on Jackson Chourio.

The cutter cuts across the zone, just outside, foul pop, now it's one ball and two strikes. Chourio's got a fresh look at the plate, trying to find rhythm. Two out, bases empty, the Brewers want to tie this one.

With the count at one and two, Rasmussen fires a 97 mile per hour four-seam fastball, ball lands in the zone, now it's two and two. Bases empty, two outs, Brewers down by two, Chourio looks to work the count.

Jackson Chourio faces Drew Rasmussen with the count at two balls and two strikes. A 96 mile per hour sinker clips the outside edge, foul pop, still two balls and two strikes. Bases empty, two outs, Brewers down by two.
Cutter at 89, just outside, foul pop. Still two balls and two strikes. Two out, bases empty, Brewers down by two. Chourio looks to work the count, but the pitch stays fair, just outside.
Sinker makes contact, just inside, good ball, now it's three and two. Chourio takes a breath, sets his stance, looks at the plate. Two outs, bases empty, Brewers down by two.
Cutter at ninety, foul, still three balls and two strikes. Chourio stays back, eyes on the plate, tries to find a crack. Two out, bases empty, Brewers down by two.

Foul pop off the inner edge, still 3 balls and 2 strikes. Chourio stays back, eyes on the plate, trying to find a crack. Two out, bases empty, Brewers down by two. Rasmussen keeps the heat on, waiting for the next pitch.
Rasmussen's been through three games, twenty-one innings, kept it tight with that 1.29 ERA, and he’s got a steady hand on the mound tonight.

Rasmussen uncorks the ninety-six mile per hour sinker, Chourio chops it hard into the dirt, Palacios fields cleanly, fires to first for the out, and that retires the side with the score staying four to two, Tampa Bay.

That brings us to the end of the second inning, with the Rays still holding a four to two lead over our Brewers. Let us pause for a brief word from our sponsors before the top of the third gets under way.
A quick tip of the cap to the wizard behind the curtain, Josh Stutting. He built this whole booth out of ones and zeros. For your technology and wizardry needs, stutting dot josh at gmail dot com.
Looking at how this series stands with the Brewers holding a one to zero lead after taking game one three to two, tonight means a great deal for both clubs.
Henderson slips the changeup, 82 miles an hour, soft and slow, it hovers just above the plate, Simpson takes it easy, swings and brushes it back to the pitcher's mound—ball. One ball, zero strikes.

Henderson drops a 81 mile per hour changeup, Simpson tries a bunt, it's missed, now the count's 1 and 1. No runner, no pressure, just the count moving along. Simpson’s got a solid start to the night, 1 for 1 so far.
Henderson sets the glove, winds up, fires a four-seam fastball, 92 miles an hour, it cuts just inside, Simpson swings and meets it—strike. Count's now one ball, two strikes.
Henderson's on the mound with 51 pitches, Simpson up to the plate, looking for a line drive—outfielders keep eyes on center, where the ball often stays when it's not carried far.
